points.description: States that the height is the length of the longest path in the tree (equivalently: the maximum path length, or the number of edges/levels on the longest downward path). Answers that give only 'the number of levels' or 'the depth of the tree' without the longest-path idea do not earn this point.
States that the path starts at the root of the tree.
States that the path ends at a leaf (a node with no children).
Makes clear the length is taken over all leaves, i.e. it is the maximum/deepest such path, not the path to some particular or arbitrary leaf.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all four ideas: longest path, starting at the root, ending at a leaf, and taken as the maximum over all leaves. Part marks are given for each of these ideas stated correctly, so an answer that says 'the longest path from root to leaf' but never says it is the maximum over leaves loses P4. No marks for answers that only restate the term (e.g. 'how tall the tree is') or that confuse height with the depth of a single node.
